short: A UUID (universally unique identifier) is a 128-bit code that identifies one document or record so that no two documents anywhere share the same identifier.
metaTitle: What is a UUID on an E-invoice? · Paper & Pen
metaDescription: A UUID is a 128-bit identifier that marks one e-invoice uniquely. Why e-invoicing rules need it and why Oman's PINT OM asks for version 5.
definition: A UUID is written as 32 hexadecimal characters in five groups, for example 8-4-4-4-12. The standard (RFC 4122) defines several versions. Version 4 is random. Version 5 is made from a name and a namespace with a hash, so the same input always gives the same UUID. On an e-invoice the UUID is separate from the invoice number. The number is for people and follows your sequence. The UUID is for systems: it lets a provider, a buyer and a tax authority recognise the same document without any doubt. Oman's PINT OM 1.0.1 requires a version 5 UUID on every invoice.

how.title: How a UUID works on an e-invoice
how.body: When your software issues the invoice, it creates the UUID and writes it into the XML. The UUID then follows the document everywhere: to your provider, to the buyer and into the tax report. A credit note or debit note quotes the UUID of the invoice it corrects. If your software sends the same invoice twice after a network error, the provider sees the same UUID and knows it is a retry, not a second sale.
items: Created once, when the invoice is issued
Quoted on every credit or debit note against the invoice
Lets a provider spot a retry of the same invoice
Stays with the document for the whole archive period

matters: A UUID protects you from two common e-invoicing problems: a duplicate invoice after a retry, and a note that cannot be matched to its invoice. Software that creates the UUID once and stores it with the issued invoice avoids both. Paper & Pen issues each e-invoice once with a version 5 UUID and keeps that UUID on the invoice.

faqs.q: Is the UUID the same as the invoice number?
faqs.a: No. The invoice number follows your own sequence and is printed for people to read. The UUID is a long system identifier that no other document shares. An e-invoice carries both. A credit note quotes the original invoice number, its date and its UUID.

faqs.q: Why does Oman ask for UUID version 5?
faqs.a: The PINT OM 1.0.1 release notes say that version 4, the random type, is no longer accepted and version 5 is required. A version 5 UUID comes from a fixed input through a hash, so the same document always gets the same identifier.
